purpose: extend the MambAtt target-domain oracle controls to FD004 so the harder multi-condition transfer headroom is quantified under the same reproduced supervised recipe
evidence_supported_conclusions: The harder multi-condition target FD004 is now covered by the same target-domain oracle control used for FD003.
Under the current reproduced MambAtt recipe, full target supervision on FD004 reaches 16.45 mean RMSE, still far below every current FD001_TO_FD004 cross-domain few-shot result.
Therefore the current FD001_TO_FD004 ceiling is not just a consequence of FD004 being intrinsically hard; substantial transfer/few-shot headroom remains relative to a target oracle.
important_caveat: The gap between the FD004 target oracle and FD001_TO_FD004 transfer results is not a pure domain-shift penalty, because full target supervision also removes the few-shot label bottleneck.
FD004 is intrinsically harder than FD001 under the current reproduced recipe, so cross-subset oracle differences should not be interpreted as direct backbone quality rankings across subsets.
next_useful_controls: Add a target-only 5-shot-without-source initialization control on FD003 and FD004 to isolate transfer initialization benefit from label scarcity.
Compare target-only 5-shot against cross-domain 5-shot under the exact same target partition seeds before proposing new loss terms.
